components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9]*$'
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Optional; stored lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the owner registered. Optional; defaults to the server's current date when omitted.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true, allows creating this owner even if another owner has the same last name
            and address (i.e. they share a household). Request-only directive; not stored.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: Server-assigned code formatted '<LAST3>-<NNNN>' - the upper-cased first three letters of the last name and a 4-digit global sequence.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007'
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: Stable identifier shared by every owner in the same household (same last name and address). Assigned when an owner is created with sharesHousehold true.
              type: string
              example: 'HH-1A2B3C4D5E6F'
              readOnly: true

## What I implemented

The spec requires the create-owner response (and subsequent GETs) to return `namesakeCount` — the number of existing owners that already shared the same `firstName` + `lastName` (case-insensitively) *before* this create. Since the acceptance test reads it back via a separate `GET /api/owners/{id}`, the value has to be **computed at create time and persisted** on the owner.

I followed the existing `customerCode`/`householdId` pattern exactly:

1. **`Owner` entity** — added a persisted `Integer namesakeCount` field (`@Column(name = "namesake_count")`) with getter/setter.

2. **Schema** — added `namesake_count INTEGER` to the `owners` table in all four dialects (h2, hsqldb — used by tests, postgres, mysql).

3. **`openapi.yml`** — added `namesakeCount` (readOnly int32, min 0) to the `Owner` schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` gets the field and MapStruct maps it automatically by name (no mapper change needed).

4. **New function `AssignOwnerNamesakeCount`** — a single-responsibility step that counts existing owners with a matching first+last name (case-insensitive, null-safe), computed before save so it never counts the new owner itself.

5. **`owners.POST.yml`** — wired the new step into the pipeline between `assignCustomerCode` and `save`, under the same `transaction` governance.

## Verification
- The new `AcceptanceTest.coreCountsNamesakes` passes (second same-named owner reports `namesakeCount == 1`).
- Full `./mvnw test` → **BUILD SUCCESS**, no regressions.

The counting logic lives in its own small function class rather than being bolted onto an existing step, keeping each function focused, and it reuses the same `OwnerRepository.findAll()` + normalized-comparison idiom already used by the duplicate-check and customer-code steps.
